summary: Landing copy built into the login screen (commit 083ee21). The operator wanted a landing surface that captures sovereignty — taking responsibility for your own identity, refusing to rent it from a company, and the circle of people who keep an identity correctly attributed and unfakeable — without leaning into government or identity-document framing. The decision: a wallet PWA has no separate marketing site, its front door IS the login screen, so the message goes into LoginPage's email step rather than a new route. The email step now opens with a small Tapit Wallet wordmark, the headline 'The record of your life belongs to you.', and a moving paragraph, then the email field below. This satisfies all three of the operator's placement instincts at once — it is persistent on every login, it is unintrusive because it simply frames the email field, and it vanishes the moment a person authenticates. A condensed one-line version was handed to the operator to paste into the Supabase sign-in email template (operator-side, not a repo file).

why.text: Operator: 'I want to have a landing page for the wallet ... capture the sovereignty ... the importance of taking responsibility for your own identity ... not requiring another company to keep up with your stuff ... a group of people around you who care about you and your identity being correctly attributed to you and not stolen or fabricated ... something simple but moving.' The operator explicitly did not want the government / ID route. The copy was drafted and approved by the operator before any code was touched, per the don't-implement-until-agreed discipline.

outcome.tests_passing: 19/19 across 5 test files (persona-contract, features-registry, library-seam, file-size, keys-never-leave). tapit-attest unchanged 82/78/0/4.
outcome.notes: [P-001] Landing copy shipped into LoginPage email step (commit 083ee21). [P-002] Form restructured so it wraps only the input and button; hero content sits outside the form. [P-003] all four gates green. Operator-side follow-up: paste the one-line email version into the Supabase template. [FEEDBACK->Foreman]: no notes — the operator gave full content direction and approved the draft before the cut, which made this a clean single-pass.

uncertainty: Gate-verified but not browser-verified — the moving paragraph is five sentences and on a narrow mobile login screen it adds real vertical height; it reads well in the markup but the operator should glance at it on a phone to confirm it does not feel heavy above the email field. Copy is a matter of taste and the operator may want it shorter or warmer after seeing it live.
